reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 32 question-paper pages and PDF pages 3–4 and 44–80 of the combined Higher Level scheme (general notes, the Paper 2 scale table on page 44, every Paper 2 model solution and marking note, and the blank closing pages). Each task boundary is the published scale, not a parser count.
sourceNotes: Candidates answer any five of Q1–6 (30 marks each) and any three of Q7–10 (50 marks each): 380 offered marks, 300 candidate marks. Every question is retained; no combined multi-question cards.
41 independently marked units. Shared scales keep their parts together: Q2(b)(i)–(ii) 15D, Q5(b)(i)–(ii) 10D, Q5(b)(iii)–(iv) 15D, Q8(b)(i)–(iii) 5C and Q10(b)(i)–(ii) 5C.
The question booklet is LC003ALP200EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003ALP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 1. All page references are PDF positions.
Q3(a) is a construction marked with a ±3 mm tolerance on the printed triangle, so it carries the calibrated measuring ruler.

Diagrams (stem-and-leaf graph, pie-chart circle, triangle t and line l, cuboid, circle sketch, cos² graph, unit circle, triangles, scatter graph, belt drive, net, lawn region) are read from the attached original question pages; prompts quote the paper’s own wording.

Scheme text layers set some letters in characters that do not match plain text (for example h as ℎ, or doubled letters in |AD|), so card rows quote only notes whose text layer matches the printed scheme; the scheme reader shows the full published notes.

cards.stem: A company makes mobile phones.
cards.questionText: The company carries out a survey on a random sample of n of their customers, where n ∈ ℕ. Based on this survey, the margin of error for the population proportion, 1/√n, is 3·4%, correct to 1 decimal place. Find one possible value of n.
solutionQuotes: Note: n = 841 to n = 891 inclusive will give correct margin of error.
Accept a correct value of n, fully verified
Note: can use margin of error between 0·0335 and 0·0345.

cards.stem: A company makes mobile phones. The company makes two types of mobile phones: an old model and a new model. A random sample of 80 of the company’s new mobile phones is tested, to see how long it takes to charge them from empty to fully charged. The mean time for this sample is 45·4 minutes, with a standard deviation of 3·1 minutes.
cards.questionText: (i) Use this information to find a 95% confidence interval for the population mean time. Give each value in your answer in minutes, correct to 1 decimal place. (ii) The mean time taken to charge the old model mobile phone from empty to fully charged is 44 minutes. The company says that the mean time taken to charge the new model mobile phone is the same as this. Using your answer to part (b)(i), or otherwise, carry out a hypothesis test at the 5% level of significance to test the company’s claim. The null hypothesis is given: The mean time taken to fully charge the new model mobile phone is 44 minutes. State clearly the alternative hypothesis, your conclusion, and the reason for your conclusion. If necessary, provide calculations.
solutionQuotes: Alternative: “The mean time taken to charge is not 44 minutes”

cards.stem: A company makes mobile phones.
cards.questionText: In a different survey, two hypothesis tests were carried out at the 5% level of significance. The p-value for the first test was 0·046. The p-value for the second test was 0·0002. Write a sentence to explain what the difference in the sizes of these p-values means about the conclusions to these two tests. You do not need to carry out any calculations.
solutionQuotes: We would have more confidence in the conclusion of the second test

cards.stem: In a game, each player wants to collect as many tokens as possible. When each player takes their turn, they roll a standard unbiased 6-sided die once. Each time they roll the die: if they roll a 1, 2, 3, or 4, they get nothing; if they roll a 5 or a 6, they get 1 token. The rules of the game are changed. Each time a player takes their turn, if they roll a 1, 2, 3, or 4, they still get nothing. If a player rolls a 5 or a 6, they have a choice. They can either: take 1 token and finish their turn; or: roll the die again, as part of the same turn. If they roll a 1, 2, 3, or 4 this time, they get nothing at all for this turn. If they roll a 5 or a 6, they get a total of 4 tokens for this turn. p is the probability that a player who gets a 5 or a 6 when they roll the die the first time will take 1 token and finish their turn, where 0 ≤ p ≤ 1.
cards.questionText: Work out the expected value (in tokens) of taking one turn using these rules. Remember that a turn can involve one or two rolls of the die. Give your answer in the form (a + bp)/9 where a, b are constants. It may be helpful to draw a tree diagram.
solutionQuotes: Note: if 1 − p is not used in Step 3, then Step 4 cannot be considered correct.
